papers.abstract: Black women with breast cancer in the US experience worse survival and lower quality of life. Addressing information needs and providing emotional and social support may improve survivorship experiences. This study evaluated feasibility and acceptability of an intervention to support Black breast cancer patients. English-speaking, Black, female breast cancer survivors diagnosed with stage I-III breast cancer within five years were invited to participate in a six-week group intervention (virtual or in-person). The intervention was adapted from the PAVING the Path to Wellness program based on a prior qualitative study. Primary endpoints were feasibility and acceptability. Exploratory endpoints included unmet information needs and well-being. Exit interviews with a subset of participants described experiences with, and benefits from, the intervention. 20 women with a mean age of 59.1 years (SD 8.2) and predominantly diagnosed at stage I (n = 11; 55%) participated. Most participants (n = 15; 88.3%) reported high levels of satisfaction and that the program provided new information relevant to their needs and helped motivate lifestyle changes. Nearly all participants (n = 15; 88.3%) expressed that it is important for other Black breast cancer survivors to receive a similar intervention. This study demonstrates proof of concept and provides insights into participant preferences. Broader-scale testing is needed to assess generalizability. NCT05700396, Registration Date: 2023-01 -17.

papers.abstract: To characterize the cancer phenotype and clinical presentation across molecularly distinct EPCAM deletion subgroups and determine how the phenotype varies with MSH2 involvement. We retrospectively evaluated 662 unrelated probands undergoing hereditary cancer multigene panel testing (MGPT) with isolated EPCAM full-gene deletions (n = 22), isolated EPCAM 3' deletions (n = 96), contiguous EPCAM full-gene deletions extending into MSH2 (n = 64), contiguous EPCAM 3' deletions extending into MSH2 (n = 116), MSH2 gross deletions (n = 155), and MSH2 nonsense/frameshift (ns/fs) variants (n = 209). Lynch syndrome (LS)-associated cancer prevalence, tumor spectrum, and PREMM5 scores were compared across cohorts. Multivariable logistic regression estimated cancer-specific associations relative to a MGPT-negative reference cohort. Isolated EPCAM full-gene deletions, comprising 18.6% of observed isolated EPCAM deletions, were not significantly associated with LS-associated cancers. The LS-associated cancer prevalence was 13.6% in this cohort, compared with 54.6% with isolated EPCAM 3' deletions and 64.1%-72.2% in MSH2-involving cohorts (P < .001). Relative to MGPT-negative individuals, isolated EPCAM 3' deletions were strongly associated with colorectal cancer (odds ratio [OR], 17.59; P < .001) but not endometrial cancer (OR, 0.76; P = .790). MSH2-involving cohorts demonstrated strong associations with both colorectal (ORs, 8.50-16.03; P < .001) and endometrial cancers (ORs, 17.31-30.47; P < .001). These findings provide new insights into the molecular and clinical heterogeneity of germline deletions involving EPCAM. Expanded detection across the full EPCAM gene and its 3' region distinguishes isolated full-gene deletions, which do not disrupt downstream MSH2 and are not associated with LS phenotypes, from isolated 3' deletions with a colorectal-predominant phenotype, and contiguous EPCAM-MSH2 deletions with an MSH2-like LS phenotype. Precise delineation of EPCAM deletion boundaries and MSH2 involvement define three clinically relevant risk groups and support more precise risk assessment, counseling, and surveillance.

papers.abstract: Local control after Gamma Knife radiosurgery (GKRS) for radioresistant brain metastases remains variable. Melanoma and renal cell carcinoma brain metastases are relatively radioresistant, yet pre-treatment prediction of local failure and its timing remains limited. We developed and internally validated a survival machine learning model to predict lesion-specific local failure and time to local failure using only pre-GKRS variables. We performed a retrospective single-center study of melanoma and renal cell carcinoma brain metastases treated with GKRS. Local failure was modeled as a right-censored survival outcome. A Random Survival Forest (RSF) was trained using baseline demographic, clinical, and tumor-level variables available before treatment. The individual lesion was the prediction unit, while data partitioning was performed at the patient level to minimize information leakage. Performance was assessed using the concordance index, cumulative/dynamic AUC, and Brier score with patient-grouped 5-fold internal cross-validation. The cohort included 893 lesions, of which 228 (25.5%) developed local failure. In the holdout test set (179 lesions), the RSF achieved a C-index of 0.842. Dynamic AUC values were 0.904, 0.890, and 0.851 at 6, 12, and 24 months, respectively, with corresponding Brier scores of 0.130, 0.153, and 0.152. Cross-validation demonstrated stable performance, with a mean C-index of 0.882. The strongest predictors were age at treatment, pre-treatment KPS, and tumor volume. Pre-treatment RSF modeling demonstrated strong internal performance for predicting local failure and time to local failure after GKRS in radioresistant brain metastases, supporting its potential for individualized risk stratification and follow-up planning. Not applicable.

papers.abstract: Breast cancer surgery is generally considered to be low risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE). However, when VTE occurs, it may lead to severe complications and increased mortality. This study aimed to determine the incidence, predictors, and clinical impact of postoperative VTE following breast cancer surgery using a large, multicenter surgical database. The American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (ACS-NSQIP) database (2008-2023) was queried to identify female patients undergoing surgery for breast cancer without concurrent reconstruction. Patients were stratified according to postoperative VTE occurrence. Demographics, comorbidities, laboratory values, operative characteristics, and 30-day outcomes were compared. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of VTE and to construct a predictive model, which was internally validated using bootstrap resampling. Among 270,564 patients included, 465 (0.2%) developed postoperative VTE. Of these, 247 (53.1%) had deep vein thrombosis, 177 (38.1%) pulmonary embolism, and 41 (8.8%) both. Patients who developed VTE were older, had higher body mass index (BMI), greater comorbidity burden, and longer operative times (all p < 0.001). They also demonstrated lower preoperative serum albumin, hematocrit, prothrombin time, and albumin-to-creatinine ratio. VTE was associated with significantly longer hospital stays, increased rates of reoperation and readmission, and a more than 20-fold higher crude 30-day mortality (1.9% vs. 0.1%) (all p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, increasing age (OR 1.26 per 10 years), BMI (OR 1.17 per 5 kg/m²), congestive heart failure (OR 2.43), metastatic cancer (OR 2.05), lower serum albumin (OR 0.63 per 1 g/dL), and longer operative duration (OR 1.09 per 30 min) were independently associated with postoperative VTE. Compared with partial mastectomy, total mastectomy (OR 2.58), modified radical mastectomy (OR 2.22), and radical mastectomy (OR 2.80) were associated with significantly higher odds of postoperative VTE. The predictive model demonstrated acceptable discrimination (AUC 0.717; optimism-corrected 0.700) and good calibration. Age, BMI, congestive heart failure, metastatic cancer, mastectomy and operative time remained associated with VTE in all sensitivity analyses. Postoperative VTE following breast cancer surgery is uncommon but associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Advanced age, obesity, cardiac comorbidity, metastatic disease, hypoalbuminemia, longer operative duration, and greater surgical extent were independently associated with increased thromboembolic risk. Awareness of these risk factors may support individualized perioperative risk assessment and thromboprophylaxis decisions, as recommended by current consensus guidance, and facilitate earlier recognition of postoperative VTE. Not applicable.

papers.abstract: Maximal safe glioma resection requires distinguishing infiltrative tumor from surrounding brain. Visible 5-aminolevulinic acid (5-ALA)-induced protoporphyrin IX (PpIX) fluorescence guides surgery, but low or heterogeneous PpIX accumulation and optical attenuation limit sensitivity. We tested whether combined fluorescence spectroscopy (FS) and diffuse reflectance spectroscopy (DRS) could improve tumor-tissue discrimination beyond visible fluorescence. Thirty-three patients with historically classified low-grade (LGG), high-grade (HGG), or recurrent glioma underwent 5-ALA-guided surgery. A handheld bimodal probe acquired in vivo FS and DRS from biopsy-paired and navigation-defined presumed non-tumor sites. A light-transport model estimated optical properties, corrected fluorescence, and quantified biomarkers. Five predictor representations were evaluated using supervised machine learning for non-tumor versus tumor discrimination and sequential LGG versus HGG classification with patient-grouped leave-one-patient-out cross-validation. Patient-clustered bootstrapping compared FS+DRS with visible fluorescence. Across 212 sites, FS+DRS achieved 85.82% sensitivity, 74.36% specificity, 80.09% balanced accuracy, and 0.81 AUROC for tumor discrimination. FS and DRS alone achieved 73.16% and 66.17% balanced accuracy, respectively. Compared with visible fluorescence, FS+DRS increased sensitivity by 34.3 percentage points (95% CI, 19.3-47.5; p < 0.001), while specificity differed by - 11.5 points (95% CI, -27.8-4.0; p = 0.2). FS+DRS detected 55/65 nonfluorescent tumor sites, including 19/23 historical LGG sites. For grade discrimination, biomarkers achieved 71.98% balanced accuracy and 0.71 AUROC. Combined FS+DRS improved tumor detection and identified histology-positive tumor not visible with standard fluorescence. Prospective multicenter evaluation should use a locked model, molecularly classified cohorts, prespecified clinical endpoints, and spatial registration to determine whether the added signal improves intraoperative decisions and patient outcomes.

papers.abstract: Relapsed B-acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) generally occurs due to the emergence of subclones resistant to therapy, leading to poor outcome. Here, we describe novel genomic alterations responsible for therapeutic resistance at a subtype level in a clinical trial (AALL1331) which randomized patients to blinatumomab and chemotherapy versus chemotherapy alone. We performed whole-genome and transcriptome sequencing on 288 patients (183 diagnosis/first relapse/germline trios and 105 additional patients with first-relapse samples) and analyzed 41 second-relapse samples. For ETV6::RUNX1, we showed that cases with gain of the fusion allele or with fusion transcript involving exon 5 of ETV6 and exon 4 of RUNX1 (E5-E4) had a higher risk of first relapse than cases with E5-E3. For the hyperdiploid subtype, we demonstrated that low modal chromosomal numbers (51-52) were more prone to first relapse than those with ≥53 chromosomes, with an additive effect of CREBBP mutations. We showed enrichment of IKZF1 alterations in the Philadelphia-like subtype and that NSD2 E1099K was commonly associated with relapse in TCF3::PBX1. Together, these new features accounted for 30% (n=55) of first relapses. Intriguingly, ~3% of relapses are related to secondary B-ALL or germline predisposition. We also compared genomic alterations at diagnosis and first relapse in relation to second relapse status in randomized patients, with TCF3::PBX1/NT5C2 linked to worse outcomes regardless of randomized arm. Together, our findings provide novel insights into the genomics of relapsed childhood B-ALL as well as in the context of blinatumomab therapy. This trial was registered at www.clinicaltrials.gov as # NCT0201853.

papers.abstract: How intracellular proteins, normally hidden from the immune system, become targets of tumor-associated antibody responses remains unresolved, as does the function of such autoantibodies encoded by tumor-infiltrating B cells (TIL-Bs). Using monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) cloned from TIL-Bs in a spontaneous hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) model, we define a class of antigens: secreted intracellular antigens (SICAs). Tumors co-opt upregulated autophagy to release cytosolic proteins, exemplified by ALDH1L1, through HSP90-mediated autophagy-dependent unconventional secretion. The resulting autoantibodies form immune complexes at the tumor site, where the SICA is locally available, recruiting and reprogramming neutrophils into tumor-associated neutrophils that drive tumor progression. Both neutrophil depletion and loss of Fcγ receptor binding abolish this effect. Autophagy-mediated SICA secretion and the corresponding autoantibody response are conserved in HCC patients and extend to lung, breast and cervical cancers. Tumors thus reshape their secretome to hijack humoral immunity, highlighting the SICA-autoantibody-FcγR axis as a potential therapeutic target.

papers.abstract: Medication taken for other reasons than for the treatment of malignant disease, termed concomitant medication, is known to affect outcomes when used with immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy and other oncological drugs. However, no research in humans has addressed the relationship between concomitant medications and efficacy of oncolytic adenovirus (OAd) therapy. We retrospectively collected medication history of 290 patients enrolled in the Advanced Therapy Access Program (ATAP), an individualized treatment program of OAds. We analyzed associations of different concomitant medications with overall survival and imaging response following therapy. Additionally, to provide further insights into mechanisms using tissue samples, we collected concomitant medication data, tumor transcriptomic data and serum proteomic data from recent Phase I clinical trials with OAd igrelimogene litadenorepvec (Ad5/3-E2F-d24-hTNF-IRES-hIL2, TILT-123). In ATAP, acetaminophen (paracetamol), opium alkaloids, anti-emetics, proton pump inhibitors, beta blockers, laxatives, and antidepressants use showed a statistical association with shorter overall survival. Use of lipid-modifying drugs (statins) and thyroid hormones showed a statistical association with better disease control in imaging. In clinical trials with TILT-123, beta blockers, anti-emetics, opioids, and benzodiazepines showed a statistical association with shorter overall survival, and lipid-modifying drugs and thyroid hormones showed a statistical association with improved disease control. Tumor transcriptomic and serum proteomic analysis showed varied temporal and locational effects on inflammatory response varying by drug class. The results provide the first human data suggesting that OAd therapy outcomes might be influenced by concomitant medications. Future studies on mechanisms of reported findings have the possibility of tailoring clinical use of OAds.

papers.abstract: Pediatric adenotonsillectomy often causes preoperative anxiety, venous cannulation pain, and emergence agitation. Esketamine has multimodal properties, but the optimal oral dose for children is unknown. This study evaluated oral esketamine at 1, 2, and 3 mg/kg for perioperative comfort. In this randomized double-blind trial, 99 children (ASA I-II, 1-6 years) received oral 10% glucose (control, n = 26) or esketamine 1 mg/kg (EK1, n = 26), 2 mg/kg (EK2, n = 23), or 3 mg/kg (EK3, n = 24) 30 min before anesthesia. Ramsay Sedation Scale (RSS) and FLACC pain score at venous cannulation, and PAED score at 15 min after extubation. remifentanil use, postoperative FLACC (2-48 h), sleep quality, and adverse events. All esketamine doses improved sedation and analgesia at cannulation (overall p < 0.001), with largest effect at 3 mg/kg. Median RSS (IQR): control 1.00 (1.00-2.00); EK1 2.00 (1.75-3.00, p = 0.028); EK2 2.00 (1.00-3.00, p = 0.049); EK3 3.00 (2.00-3.37, p < 0.001). FLACC scores: control 6.00 (3.00-7.00); EK1 2.50 (1.00-4.00, p = 0.016); EK2 2.00 (0.00-4.00, p = 0.001); EK3 0.00 (0.00-1.75, p < 0.001). PAED score at 15 min was lower in EK2 than control (5.00 [2.00-10.00] vs. 10.00 [6.00-12.00], p = 0.048). Remifentanil consumption was reduced in EK3 (120.00 [80.00-159.50] vs. 240.00 [160.00-315.00] μg, p = 0.001). Postoperative pain at 2-6 h was lower in EK2 and EK3 (p < 0.05), persisting to 48 h in EK3 (p < 0.05). Sleep quality improved in EK3 at 24 h (p = 0.023) and 48 h (p = 0.032). Adverse events did not differ significantly. Preoperative oral esketamine (1-3 mg/kg) enhances perioperative comfort in children undergoing adenotonsillectomy. The 2 mg/kg dose offers the best balance of efficacy and safety, while 3 mg/kg provides superior analgesia and opioid sparing.

papers.abstract: In 2025, Endometrial cancer (EC) is the 6th most common cancer in women globally, with rising cases in younger patients and communities of color. EC risk factors include postmenopausal status, family history, diabetes, and hyperestrogenic state conditions. We retrospectively reviewed charts of patients who received hysterectomies or hysteroscopies for either cancerous and/or benign diagnoses between 2016 and 2021 at a university hospital in Phoenix (AZ). Sociodemographic and clinical data were collected. The Arizona Social Vulnerability Index was utilized to understand contributors to EC diagnosis outcomes. Kruskal-Wallis, Fisher's exact, and multinomial logistic regression tests were used to compare EC to benign conditions. Two hundred sixty-one patients were diagnosed with benign conditions (n = 31), hyperplasia (n = 53), or EC (n = 168). EC patients were older (p = 0.016), mostly post-menopausal (p = 0.008), and more frequently had diabetes (p = 0.001) compared to patients with benign conditions. Native Americans had a higher percentage of EC cases relative to other races (p = 0.07) and presented with EC at significantly younger ages (49.79 years, p = 0.001) and with more comorbid diagnoses of diabetes (38.5%, p = 0.051) compared to Whites (61.99 years, 27.1%). Hispanic patients also presented with EC at younger ages (53.74,p = 0.006) compared to non-Hispanics (61.56 years). Higher vulnerability in Housing Type and Transportation scores (p = 0.045) among patients diagnosed with EC was observed. Public health initiatives should target modifiable risk factors contributing to increased EC rates at younger ages, especially in Native American and Hispanic communities. Differences in housing and transportation highlight social structures and health accessibility as areas for improving EC outcomes.

papers.abstract: Lip and oral cavity cancer (LOCC) represents a significant global health burden, with varying incidence rates across regions and populations. Understanding these trends is crucial for effective resource allocation and the development of targeted public health interventions. We extracted LOCC incidence data from the GBD 2021 study, covering the period from 1990 to 2021. Age-standardized incidence rates (ASRs) were calculated, and temporal trends were assessed across geographical and socioeconomic strata. The Estimated Annual Percentage Change (EAPC) was calculated to assess temporal trends. A Bayesian age-period-cohort (BAPC) model was applied to predict future incidence rates up to 2040 under the scenario of unchanged population-level risk-factor exposure and no large-scale public-health interventions. Global new LOCC cases reached 421.6 thousand in 2021, up by 142.2% relative to 1990; the global ASR increased 0.40% annually to 4.9 per 100,000. Regional disparities were striking: South Asia, Australasia and Eastern Europe bore the highest ASRs, while several high-income countries showed decreasing incidence. Females demonstrated a higher EAPC of ASR compared with males. National-level trends could not be directly predicted by sociodemographic index. In the absence of effective interventions, the global ASR is projected to rise to 5.26 per 100,000 and new cases to 610.1 thousand by 2040. The global incidence of LOCC has increased significantly over the past three decades, with substantial regional variations. Effective prevention and early detection strategies are crucial for reducing the incidence and improving outcomes for LOCC globally.

papers.abstract: Obinutuzumab-based regimens are established frontline treatments for chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), but infusion-related reactions (IRRs) and prolonged administration increase patient burden and outpatient chair occupancy. Evidence on shortened obinutuzumab infusion in CLL remains limited. To evaluate the safety, feasibility, and clinical outcomes of a 2-h obinutuzumab infusion protocol in treatment-naïve CLL. This retrospective single-center cohort study included 112 treatment-naïve patients receiving venetoclax-obinutuzumab (n = 72) or obinutuzumab-chlorambucil (n = 40). From cycle 1 day 8 onward, patients were managed according to either a shortened-infusion strategy (Short; n = 64) or a standard-duration strategy (Long; n = 48). The primary outcome was IRR incidence and severity; secondary outcomes included chair time, response rate, and progression-free survival. IRR rates did not differ significantly between the Short and Long groups (71.9% vs. 83.3%; odds ratio, 0.51; 95% confidence interval, 0.17-1.41; p = 0.18). Most IRRs occurred during the first infusion (87.4%), before implementation of the shortened protocol. Because cycle 1 day 1 and day 2 were administered using the same standard protocol in both groups, the safety comparison relevant to the shortened-infusion strategy begins at cycle 1 day 8; IRRs were infrequent from cycle 1 day 8 onward, and none occurred from cycle 1 day 15 onward, when eligible patients in the Short group were receiving the 2-h infusion. Grade 2 reactions predominated (91.6%); no Grade 4 IRRs occurred among the 112 patients included in the analysis. The shortened protocol saved 1.8 h per visit and 11.2 h per patient (42%). No apparent adverse signal in response or progression-free survival was observed. In frontline CLL care, a 2-h obinutuzumab infusion from cycle 1 day 8 was feasible, safe, and substantially reduced chair time, supporting its use to improve outpatient treatment efficiency.

papers.abstract: Treatment decisions in older patients with mature B-cell lymphoproliferative disorders (MBLD) are frequently guided by chronological age and comorbidity burden, although their ability to predict clinically relevant outcomes remains uncertain. We conducted a retrospective real-world study including 172 patients with MBLD between 2016 and 2021, assessing the association of age and comorbidity burden (standardised using the Cumulative Illness Rating Scale for Geriatrics, CIRS-G score) with treatment intensity, toxicity, and clinical outcomes. Treatment intensity decreased significantly with both age (p = 0.003) and CIRS-G score (p < 0.001). However, neither age nor CIRS-G score was associated with an increased rate of treatment-related toxic events. In contrast, older age was associated with worse overall survival and lower response rates (all p < 0.05), whereas CIRS-G score was not significantly associated with these outcomes. Similar associations between age and outcomes were observed in the DLBCL subgroup. In this real-world cohort of patients with MBLD, chronological age was more consistently associated with treatment patterns and clinical outcomes than comorbidity burden as measured by the CIRS-G score. These findings suggest that chronological age alone may not adequately capture the heterogeneity of older patients and support the use of more comprehensive assessments of frailty and functional status to inform treatment decisions.

papers.abstract: To assess whether high-grade components occupying < 20% of the tumor have prognostic value and whether an Adjusted Grade nomogram improves risk stratification in Stage I invasive lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). We retrospectively analyzed 1539 patients with pathologically confirmed Stage I invasive LUAD undergoing R0 resection; 1321 with follow-up, including 967 with preoperative CT. Tumors were classified by IASLC Grade and reclassified according to predominant pattern and high-grade components; Adjusted Grade 3 was subdivided into MHGC ≤ 5%, DHGC > 5% to < 20%, and SHGC ≥ 20%. Cox models identified DFS predictors. Nomograms were internally validated with 1000 bootstrap resamples and assessed for discrimination, calibration, and net benefit. During a median 38-month follow-up, 124 DFS events occurred. Adjusted Grade 3 independently predicted recurrence (HR 3.07, 95% CI 1.54-6.12), while MHGC and DHGC were associated with poorer DFS (HR 3.95, 95% CI 1.53-10.15; HR 2.55, 95% CI 1.12-5.80). In the CT subgroup, consolidation-to-tumor ratio (CTR) independently predicted DFS (HR 3.08, 95% CI 1.46-6.51). Optimism-corrected C-index was 0.740 for the Adjusted Grade-based nomogram, compared with 0.727 for the IASLC-based nomogram and 0.612 for TNM staging. After adding CTR, they were 0.763 and 0.745 for the Adjusted Grade- and IASLC-based nomogram. Decision-curve analysis showed similar net benefit profiles for the two nomograms. High-grade components below 20% were associated with poorer DFS. papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer (OC) remains the most lethal gynaecological malignancy, and acquired resistance to PARP inhibitors such as olaparib represents a major clinical challenge. Although dysregulation of iron metabolism has been implicated in tumorigenesis, the specific role of the iron exporter SLC40A1 (ferroportin, FPN) in mediating olaparib resistance remains poorly understood. The study aimed to elucidate the clinical significance of FPN deficiency and to explore therapeutic strategies for reversing olaparib resistance. FPN expression was evaluated in OC samples from a clinical cohort of 19 patients, stratified by olaparib responsiveness, to determine its prognostic value. Functional mechanisms were investigated using multiple OC cell lines, patient-derived organoids (PDOs), and mouse xenograft models. We integrated analyses of iron homeostasis, ROS dynamics, DNA repair capacity, and innate immune signaling, with a focus on the cGAS-STING-STAT3 signaling cascade. The therapeutic potential of combining olaparib with the ferroptosis inducer erastin or the STING inhibitor C-176 was assessed as a strategy to overcome FPN deficiency-driven resistance. Clinically, FPN expression was significantly downregulated in olaparib-resistant tissues compared with sensitive controls (p < 0.05), and low FPN levels were strongly associated with poor therapeutic outcomes. Mechanistically, FPN deficiency promoted intracellular iron accumulation and ROS generation, which led to increased ferroptosis vulnerability, impaired homologous recombination repair (HRR) and concomitant activation of the cGAS-STING-STAT3 inflammatory axis, thereby driving olaparib resistance. Notably, in vivo studies demonstrated that combining olaparib with either erastin or C-176 significantly suppressed tumour growth and restored drug sensitivity compared with monotherapy (p < 0.01), supporting the translational potential of targeting this axis. Our study establishes a clinically relevant mechanistic connection between ferroportin deficiency and cGAS-STING-STAT3-mediated olaparib resistance in OC. We identify the FPN-ROS-cGAS-STING-STAT3 axis as an actionable vulnerability in resistant OC, indicating that this pathway is a promising therapeutic target to overcome olaparib resistance. FPN loss drives olaparib resistance and predicts poor outcomes in ovarian cancer. FPN loss causes iron and ROS accumulation, impairing HRR and activating the cGAS-STING-STAT3 axis. The cGAS-STING-STAT3 pro-survival program drives olaparib resistance. STING inhibition restores olaparib sensitivity in resistant ovarian cancer.

papers.abstract: c-MET is implicated in ESCC progression, but whether c-MET inhibition reshapes immune checkpoint expression and the tumor immune microenvironment remains unclear. ESCC cell lines were treated with Tepotinib, and c-MET and PD-L1 expression were examined by Western blotting and immunofluorescence. MET knockdown was performed in TE-1 and KYSE150 cells. AKR syngeneic subcutaneous tumor models were used to assess PD-L1 and PD-1 expression, immune cell composition, transcriptomic and proteomic changes, NF-κB/p65 signaling, and the efficacy of Tepotinib combined with an anti-PD-1 antibody. Tepotinib decreased c-MET expression and increased PD-L1 expression in ESCC cells. MET knockdown produced a similar increase in PD-L1. In vivo, Tepotinib increased PD-L1 and PD-1 expression in tumor tissues and increased PD-L1 expression in the CD45- non-immune compartment, together with decreased CD8+ T cells and cDC1 cells, increased Treg cells, and increased CD206 expression in tumor-associated macrophages. Dual immunofluorescence and quantitative analysis further showed an increased proportion of CD8+PD-1+ cells among total CD8+ cells in Tepotinib-treated tumors. Transcriptomic and proteomic analyses indicated enrichment of inflammatory and immune-related pathways, including NF-κB, TNF, JAK-STAT, and immune checkpoint-related signaling. Tepotinib increased p65 phosphorylation, whereas NF-κB inhibition reduced p-p65 and PD-L1 expression. Tepotinib combined with anti-PD-1 antibody reduced tumor burden and delayed humane endpoint events compared with monotherapy. c-MET inhibition is accompanied by adaptive PD-L1 upregulation and immunosuppression-related changes in the tumor microenvironment in ESCC. NF-κB/p65 signaling may participate in this response. The enhanced antitumor activity observed with Tepotinib plus anti-PD-1 therapy supports further investigation of this combination strategy.

papers.abstract: Cervical cancer (CC) remains a major global health challenge characterized by high incidence and mortality. The histone methyltransferase suppressor of variegation 3-9 homolog 1 (SUV39H1) has emerged as a key epigenetic regulator in tumor progression, but its role in modulating pyroptosis and remodeling of the immune microenvironment in CC remains unclear. In this study, we demonstrate that SUV39H1 promotes CC progression through dual epigenetic regulation, specifically repression of gasdermin E (GSDME) and activation of chemokine (C-X-C motif) ligand 10 (CXCL10). Overexpression of SUV39H1 in HeLa and SiHa cells enhanced histone 3 lysine 9 tri methylation (H3K9me3) deposition at the DFNA5 (GSDME) promoter, resulting in reduced transcription and suppressed GSDME-dependent pyroptosis-like cell death. Interestingly, it also upregulated CXCL10 expression. Functional assays confirmed that SUV39H1 attenuated GSDME-mediated pyroptosis-like cell death and enhanced cell migration via induction of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Moreover, SUV39H1 drives CXCL10 secretion, which activates the chemokine (C-X-C motif) receptor 3 (CXCR3) signaling axis in macrophages and upregulates immunosuppressive molecules including programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1), T cell immunoglobulin and mucin-domain containing-3 (Tim-3), and secreted phosphoprotein 1 (SPP1), thereby fostering an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME), and these effects appear parallel to GSDME suppression. Collectively, these findings reveal a multifaceted oncogenic role of SUV39H1 in CC, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target for epigenetic and immunomodulatory intervention.

papers.abstract: The integration of anthracyclines with HER2-targeted agents in neoadjuvant therapy for HER2-positive breast cancer has been limited by cardiotoxicity concerns. This randomized phase II METIS trial (NCT04172259) assessed whether concurrent pegylated liposomal doxorubicin (PLD)-containing chemotherapy plus dual HER2 blockade (trastuzumab/pertuzumab) could improve efficacy without increasing cardiac risk. A total of 156 patients with stage II-III HER2-positive breast cancer were randomized to a PLD-based concurrent regimen or an epirubicin and cyclophosphamide (EC)-based sequential regimen. The PLD-based concurrent group achieved a higher pathological complete response (pCR) rate (67.5% vs. 48.7%; difference, 18.8%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 3.6-34.0; P = 0.033) compared with the EC-based sequential group, with greater benefit in hormone receptor-positive disease (58.7% vs. 36.7%) and stage II tumors (82.1% vs. 48.0%). After a median follow-up of 37.5 months, fewer event-free survival (EFS) events occurred in the PLD-based concurrent group (3 vs. 8), yielding a hazard ratio (HR) of 0.35 (95% CI, 0.09-1.32; P = 0.105). The estimated 3-year EFS rates were 96.0% (95% CI, 88.1-98.7) versus 90.7% (95% CI, 81.5-95.6). Achieving pCR was significantly associated with improved EFS (HR = 0.15; 95% CI, 0.03-0.71; P = 0.006). Cardiac safety was comparable, with no symptomatic cardiac dysfunction and only one grade ≥3 cardiotoxicity in the EC-based sequential group. These findings support PLD-based concurrent therapy with trastuzumab and pertuzumab as an effective and safe neoadjuvant option for high-risk HER2-positive breast cancer, warranting further evaluation in phase III trials.

papers.abstract: Chronic antibody-mediated rejection (CAMR) is a leading cause of late kidney allograft failure and shares features of chronic immune activation with systemic autoimmune diseases, but how circulating immune states connect to spatially organized graft injury and whether related immune features recur in autoimmune inflammation remain unclear. Here, we integrated single-cell profiles from peripheral blood and kidney graft samples from patients with CAMR or stable allograft function and healthy controls with independent transplant cohorts, bulk transcriptomic datasets, spectral flow cytometry, multiplex immunofluorescence, high-resolution spatial transcriptomics, and a large blood immune reference spanning autoimmune and inflammatory diseases. CAMR was associated with reproducible myeloid expansion and enrichment of SLC8A1+ monocytes/macrophages, ANK3+CD4+ memory T cells, ZEB2hi T cells, and CD16+ NK cells. These subsets showed migratory and tissue-interacting transcriptional features, including recurrent CXCR4 and ZEB2 expression, suggesting candidate immune states potentially linked to local graft immune organization. In graft tissue, CXCL12-expressing fibroblasts and CXCR4-expressing immune cells were increased in CAMR. High-resolution spatial transcriptomics localized this fibroblast-immune architecture to perivascular regions marked by endothelial activation and stromal remodeling and placed CAMR-associated immune states within adjacent immune-rich neighborhoods, supporting a CXCL12-CXCR4 axis that may be associated with local immune accumulation. Comparisons with large-scale blood immune reference data and spatial transcriptomic datasets from rheumatoid arthritis and systemic lupus erythematosus suggested partial recurrence of related immune states and fibroblast-immune organization. Together, this study links circulating CAMR immune remodeling to a spatially organized CXCL12-CXCR4 fibroblast-immune niche and suggests that elements of this niche recur across alloimmune and autoimmune inflammation.

papers.abstract: Clinical outcomes after CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy in patients with relapsed or refractory (r/r) diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) remain heterogeneous, underscoring the need for improved risk stratification. As CAR T-cell efficacy is shaped not only by tumor-intrinsic features, host-related factors may also contribute to outcome variability. The spleen, the largest secondary lymphoid organ and a key regulator of immune cell trafficking, is a biologically plausible yet underexplored imaging marker in this setting. We retrospectively analyzed 88 patients with r/r DLBCL and available baseline imaging who received commercial CD19-directed CAR T-cell products between September 2019 and July 2025. Spleen volume was analyzed as a continuous variable (per 100 mL), without dichotomization or prespecified cutoffs, and clinical outcomes were examined in relation to baseline spleen volume. With a median follow-up of 24.4 months, 2-year progression-free survival and overall survival were 40.9% and 56.4%, respectively. Higher baseline spleen volume was associated with inferior overall survival, a higher cumulative incidence of relapse/progression, and inferior post-progression survival. The 24-month risk of death increased progressively with increasing spleen volume. Baseline spleen volume remained independently associated with inferior overall survival after adjustment for established pretreatment risk factors (aHR 1.136 per 100 mL, 95% CI, 1.012-1.275; p = 0.030). Findings were consistent in sensitivity analyses including adjustment for BMI and after exclusion of patients with splenic lymphoma manifestations. Baseline spleen volume thus emerges as a readily available imaging-derived marker that could complement established risk factors and refine baseline risk stratification prior to CAR T-cell therapy in r/r DLBCL. Beyond the pretreatment setting, it also has potential utility for prognostication after relapse/progression.

papers.abstract: Against the background of therapeutic improvements and centralization of care, we evaluated epidemiological trends in Ewing and Ewing-like sarcomas (ES) among children and young adolescents in the Netherlands over three decades. Data on 464 pediatric patients (0-17 years) diagnosed with ES in the Netherlands between 1990 and 2018 were obtained from the Netherlands Cancer Registry, with follow-up until February 2024. Incidence trends were evaluated by calculating the average annual percentage change (AAPC). A Cox regression model was used to assess the effect of sex, age, stage at diagnosis, and tissue-specific tumor site on changes in 5-year observed overall survival (OS) over time. Between 1990 and 2018, on average 16 pediatric patients were diagnosed with ES yearly. The age-standardized incidence rate increased by 2.1% annually, rising from 3.7 per million person-years in 1990-1999 to 5.2 in 2010-2018. Over time, the use of local therapy combined with chemotherapy increased from 75% in 1990-1999 to 94% in 2010-2018. Five-year OS improved from 56% (1990-1999) to 70% (2010-2018), and the 10-year OS increased from 51% to 65% in these periods. Multivariable analyzes confirmed a lower risk of mortality from ES in 2010-2018 (HR 0.4, 95% CI 0.3-0.6) compared to 1990-1999. ES incidence increased alongside improved survival, likely influenced by various factors, including advancements in diagnostics, treatment, supportive care, and follow-up. Nevertheless, patients with metastatic disease and older children continue to experience higher mortality risks, highlighting the importance of ongoing research and targeted treatments to further improve pediatric ES outcomes.

papers.abstract: Brain metastasis remains a major cause of mortality and treatment failure in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, current models of cerebral dissemination rarely integrate microbiome-dependent systemic and intratumoral biology.This Review examines the potential microbiome-brain metastasis axis linking gut, lung, and intratumoral microbial communities to intracranial dissemination and therapeutic response. A reproducible literature search was conducted to evaluate proposed mechanisms underlying microbiome-associated brain metastasis. Evidence for each mechanistic claim was graded using a four-level evidence scheme (E1-E4), while microbial detection confidence was assessed using a four-tier hierarchy (D1-D4). No component of the proposed axis reached E1 evidence, and all published microbial observations in NSCLC brain metastasis rests on nucleic-acid detection alone. Five mechanisms are examined: circulating microbial metabolites acting on endothelial permeability and glial reactivity; microbiome-imprinted immune-cell trafficking;intracellular bacteria within primary lung tumours; cross-kingdom MR1/MAIT and Dectin-CARD9 signalling; and candidate host genetic determinants. The available human data are small, single-centre and cross-sectional, reporting association with brain-metastasis status rather than prediction or causation; that bacteria accompany disseminating tumour cells into the brain remains a hypothesis awaiting paired sampling, spatial localization and experimental perturbation.We therefore reserve the term prevention for proposed trials, integrate microbial features with established molecular risk models, and specify the genetic-perturbation program and research-only decision pathway that would convert these claims into E1 evidence. The microbiome-brain metastasis axis provides a hypothesis-generating framework for investigating microbial contributions to cerebral dissemination. Multi-centre validation, paired primary-brain metastasis profiling and gnotobiotic models are required before microbiome-directed strategies can be said to improve intracranial outcomes;until then this framework is hypothesis-generating, not practice-changing. The proposed microbiome-brain metastasis axis links gut, lung and intratumoral microbial communities to intracranial dissemination in NSCLC. Current evidence remains insufficient to establish causality, with no proposed mechanism reaching the highest evidence level (E1). Five candidate mechanisms involve microbial metabolites, immune-cell trafficking, intratumoral bacteria, MR1/MAIT and Dectin-CARD9 signalling, and host genetic determinants. Multicentre validation, paired primary and brain metastasis profiling, spatial microbial localisation and experimental perturbation are needed to establish causality and assess clinical relevance. Microbiome-directed prevention and therapeutic strategies remain investigational and should not yet inform routine clinical practice.

papers.abstract: In recent years, significant progress has been made in developing targeted therapy for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, these therapies are only applicable to specific NSCLC groups with corresponding gene mutations. Therefore, developing novel targeted therapies to benefit more patients remains an important task. Our prior work demonstrated that LKB1-mutant NSCLC cells are highly susceptible to cell death induced by glucose starvation. In this study, we investigated a novel combinational therapeutic strategy utilizing a sodium-glucose co-transporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitor canagliflozin and a covalent KRASG12C inhibitor adagrasib, two clinically approved therapeutics, to selectively target LKB1-KRASG12C co-mutated NSCLC. First, we verified the co-occurrence of LKB1 and KRAS mutations in clinical NSCLC cohorts. Second, compared to other SGLT2 inhibitors, canagliflozin induced higher cytotoxicity in LKB1-mutant cells, and SGLT2 knockdown partially attenuated this effect. Mechanistically, the high susceptibility to canagliflozin was associated with impaired activation of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK). Furthermore, canagliflozin suppressed mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) activity and robustly inhibited cell growth in LKB1-mutant models in vitro. Third, adagrasib exhibited selective cytotoxicity in KRASG12C-mutated NSCLC. Finally, the combination of canagliflozin and adagrasib synergistically reduced cell viability in LKB1-KRASG12C co-mutated H23 and H2122 cells in vitro. Importantly, canagliflozin attenuated the adaptive MAPK signaling rebound induced by adagrasib in vitro. The therapeutic potential of this combination was confirmed in an H2122 nude mouse xenograft model in vivo. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that a combination of canagliflozin and adagrasib suppresses LKB1-KRASG12C co-mutated NSCLC, laying a solid preclinical foundation for developing a new therapeutic strategy for this group of NSCLC.

papers.abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction is frequently well-known to induce mitochondrial dysfunction-associated senescence (MIDAS), a specialized form of cellular senescence marked by a distinct senescent phenotype. Sirtuin-3 (SIRT3) is a key regulator of mitochondrial function through its deacetylase activity, and emerging evidence highlights that its deficiency induces MIDAS in fibroblasts. However, the precise mechanism by which SIRT3 regulates MIDAS, as well as the role of MIDAS in tumorigenesis, remains incompletely understood. Here, we report that SIRT3 deficiency inhibits colorectal cancer (CRC) progression by inducing MIDAS. Mechanistically, SIRT3 deacetylates the mitochondrial carrier SLC25A13 at lysine 568. SIRT3 loss triggers K568 hyperacetylation, impairing SLC25A13 function and disrupting the malate-aspartate shuttle. This cascade reduces the cytosolic NAD+/NADH ratio, activating the AMPK-p53 axis to initiate MIDAS. Clinically, low levels of SLC25A13-K568 acetylation are associated with poor prognosis in human CRC. Furthermore, senolytic treatment selectively eliminates these senescent cells and suppresses tumor growth. Our findings unveil a SIRT3-SLC25A13 axis governing NAD+/NADH homeostasis and MIDAS, revealing a potential therapeutic strategy for CRC.

papers.abstract: PD-(L)1×VEGF bispecific antibodies integrate immune checkpoint blockade and VEGF inhibition within a single molecule, offering a potential strategy to overcome angiogenesis-associated immune resistance. At the 2026 ASCO Annual Meeting, the randomized phase 3 HARMONi-6 trial demonstrated an overall survival benefit with ivonescimab plus chemotherapy over tislelizumab plus chemotherapy in previously untreated advanced squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), extending survival evidence to an active PD-1-based first-line comparator. Exploratory phase 2 studies of pumitamig, SSGJ-707, and HB0025 reported encouraging activity in first-line NSCLC, while phase 1 and 2 studies of IMM2510 and ivonescimab-based regimens suggested activity after prior immunotherapy. Smaller exploratory studies also reported activity in perioperative head and neck cancer, colorectal cancer, endometrial cancer, and mucosal melanoma. Collectively, these findings highlight the clinical potential of PD-(L)1×VEGF bispecific antibodies, with the strongest evidence in first-line squamous NSCLC and broader applications remaining hypothesis-generating. Future development should prioritize predictive biomarkers, resistance mechanisms, optimal treatment sequencing, and careful assessment of immune-related and VEGF-associated toxicities.

papers.abstract: Quality metrics are quantifiable measures that are used to assess healthcare processes and outcomes. Gynecologic oncologists encounter quality measures in their daily practice. These include measures associated with different phases or episodes of care including inpatient care, surgical care and cancer care. Common examples include surgical complication rates, rates of chemotherapy-related adverse events and broader institutional metrics such as length of stay, readmissions and mortality. Measures can be used for different purposes including direct quality improvement, payment reform, accreditation, public reporting and external rankings. While quality metrics can drive standardization and improve performance, they can increase administrative burden and cause unintended consequences. In this review, we discuss commonly encountered metrics in gynecologic oncology, first by general metrics and then by specific disease sites. In cases where specific disease site metrics do not exist, the best available evidence for high value care in gynecologic oncology is summarized. papers.abstract: Complete gross tumor resection is an important prognostic factor in advanced ovarian cancer (AOC), and total parietal peritonectomy (TPP) is a key method to achieve it. Despite undergoing complete gross resection, some patients experience thoracic recurrence, which is associated with a poor prognosis. Clinicopathological factors associated with such recurrence remain unclear. We hypothesized that occult lymphovascular invasion within the subdiaphragmatic peritoneum, the lymphatic interface between the peritoneal and thoracic cavities, may be associated with thoracic recurrence. We retrospectively analyzed patients with International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics stage IIIB-IVB ovarian cancer who underwent complete resection using TPP. Clinicopathological factors evaluated were stage, neoadjuvant chemotherapy, homologous recombination deficiency status, and intraoperative macroscopic findings. The subdiaphragmatic regions were microscopically assessed for lymphovascular invasion using D2-40 and CD31 immunohistochemistry. Thoracic recurrence was analyzed using Fine-Gray model. Seventy-four patients were included: 47 (63.5%) and 27 (36.5%) had stage III and IV disease, respectively. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy was administered to 38 (51.4%) patients. Subdiaphragmatic lymphatic invasion (SLI) was detected in 37 patients (50.0%), including seven without macroscopic lesions; venous invasion was rare (n = 1). During a median follow-up of 30.9 months, 20 (27.0%) and 18 (24.3%) patients developed thoracic and abdominal recurrence, respectively. Thoracic recurrence was significantly higher with SLI (43.2% vs. 10.8%); SLI independently predicted thoracic recurrence (subdistribution hazard ratios, 16.5, 95% confidence interval, 5.1-53.9; p < 0.001). SLI was independently associated with thoracic recurrence after complete gross resection in AOC, supporting a potential transdiaphragmatic pathway of tumor dissemination.

papers.abstract: To assess the association between human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination following cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) and subsequent invasive cervical cancer (CC) diagnoses. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. Patients diagnosed with CIN (ICD-10-CM: N87, N87.0, N87.1, D06) during 2020-2022 who underwent regular cervical screening (Z12.4) were compared according to subsequent HPV vaccination records. Propensity score matching (PSM) incorporated demographic characteristics, selected diagnosis, and cervical procedures. Outcomes were assessed for day 1 through year 3 after the CIN diagnosis. Patients with CC recorded before diagnosis were excluded. Exploratory analyses evaluated code-defined CIN1-2 and CIN3 subgroups. Matching yielded 7397 patients per cohort. After outcome-specific exclusions, 7194 vaccinated patients and 7233 comparators remained, with 47 and 92 CC diagnoses, respectively (HR 0.56, 95% CI 0.39-0.79; p=0.001). By CIN grade, a significant association was observed in CIN3 patients (HR 0.32; 95% CI 0.20-0.53; p < 0.001), but not CIN1-2 patients (HR 0.98; 95% CI 0.51-1.92; p=0.96). Recorded HPV vaccination was associated with fewer CC diagnosis overall and in CIN3 patients. Exposure misclassification, residual confounding, differential observation, and non-proportional hazards limit casual interpretation.

papers.abstract: Most endometrial cancers (EC) are obesity-related; yet, there is little known about utilization of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RAs), which are effective weight loss medications, in EC. This is a retrospective cohort study using TriNetX US Collaborative Network, a de-identified, longitudinal electronic health record dataset. Female patients were identified from 1/1/2018-4/15/2024 with BMI ≥30 and grouped by presence or absence of EC diagnosis. Patients were followed for two years or up to 4/15/26, whichever came first. These two groups were 1:1 propensity score matched for demographics, BMI, and comorbidities. Patients with prior bariatric surgery or GLP-1RA use were excluded. The primary outcome was GLP-1RA use. Subgroup analysis was conducted among patients with BMI ≥40. From 2018 to 2024, GLP-1RAs use in both cohorts increased. However, utilization was consistently lower among patients with EC. In 2018, GLP-1RA use was 1.0% among patients with EC vs. 1.2% among those without EC (RR 0.82, CI 0.60-1.13). By 2024, use increased to 7.8% and 10.6%, respectively (RR 0.73, CI 0.61-0.87). Similar findings were observed among patients with a BMI ≥40, with significantly faster uptake of GLP-1RAs among women without EC. Patients with EC were less likely to receive GLP-1RAs than matched patients without EC despite obesity being a major risk factor for EC. These findings highlight a potential gap in obesity management among EC survivors and support further investigation of the safety and efficacy of GLP-1RAs in this population.

papers.abstract: Adjuvant chemotherapy (ACT) indication in stage II colorectal cancer (CRC) remains challenging, as clinical, pathological, and ctDNA inadequately predict benefit. Immune infiltration correlates with outcome, yet transcriptional signatures have not been systematically evaluated in prospective trial cohorts. We aimed to identify a prognostic transcriptional signature in high-risk stage II CRC patients treated with ACT within the TOSCA trial. From the TOSCA trial, 124 high-risk stage II patients were selected using a matched case-control design, with matching based on center, pT stage, ACT regimen, and treatment duration. Whole-transcriptome sequencing was performed on FFPE samples. MSI status was inferred bioinformatically. Prognostic associations were assessed using log-rank tests and multivariable Cox models adjusting for MSI status and tumor sidedness. Seventy-two samples met RNA quality criteria. Median follow-up was 70.9 months; 40% were right-sided, 60% received FOLFOX, 54% 3-month ACT, and 19% were MSI-high. Transcriptomic analyses highlighted immune-regulatory and TGF-β/stromal programs associated with outcome. A biologically defined Immune Exclusion (IE) phenotype, characterized by low ICR and high Hallmark TGF-β signaling, was observed in approximately 28% of patients and was associated with shorter DFS (HR=2.22, p = 0.036). This association persisted after adjustment for MSI status and tumor sidedness (HR=2.47, p = 0.018). A reduced seven-gene IE signature (rIE) was subsequently derived and was also associated with shorter DFS after multivariable adjustment (HR=2.83, p = 0.012). The IE phenotype and its reduced rIE signature were associated with shorter DFS in high-risk stage II colon cancer and represent exploratory candidate prognostic biomarkers requiring validation in independent cohorts. Identifying stage II colorectal cancer (CRC) patients who will relapse despite standard adjuvant chemotherapy (ACT) remains an unmet clinical need. Current clinicopathological and ctDNA-based approaches do not fully resolve risk stratification in this setting. In this study, whole-transcriptome profiling of high-risk stage II CRC from the prospective TOSCA trial identified an Immune Exclusion (IE) signature associated with significantly shorter disease-free survival, which remained associated with DFS after adjustment for MSI status and tumor sidedness. These findings provide a biological framework for further validation in independent cohorts and for future hypothesis-generating studies aimed at refining risk stratification and exploring alternative therapeutic approaches.

papers.abstract: We previously reported CAMKV-IgG paraneoplastic encephalitis accompanying uterine and neuroendocrine-lineage carcinomas. Here, we describe 7 new cases (12 total) and report CSF cytokine/chemokine profiles and coexisting antibody frequency. Patient samples demonstrating the CAMKV-specific murine tissue-based indirect immunofluorescence assay (TIIFA) staining pattern were tested by protein microarray and confirmed CAMKV-specific cell-based assay. CSF cytokines/chemokines were analyzed in 4 patients. Median symptom-onset age was 69 years (range 53-79); 8/12 were women. Common manifestations included altered mental status (7/12), hyperkinetic movements (6/12), seizures (5/12), psychiatric, and insomnia (4/12 each). Five patients had coexisting antibodies: tripartite motif-containing protein-9 (3), N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor (2), antineuronal nuclear antibody-type-1 (ANNA-1) and γ-aminobutyric acid B receptor (1 each). All 12 had cancer, including adenocarcinoma (6/12; uterine 4, lung 1, prostate 1), lymphoma (Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin), or other carcinoma (urothelial, Merkel cell, hepatocellular, and poorly differentiated (1 each). All 3 available cancers (uterine, 2; prostate adenocarcinoma, 1) were immunohistochemistry positive for CAMKV. 6/8 had CSF lymphocytic pleocytosis. MRIs revealed mesial temporal and basal ganglia T2 hyperintensities in 6/10 and 5/10, respectively. Among 7 immunotherapy-treated patients, 6 improved initially, although 5/7 with follow-up died from cancer. CSF IL-13 and GM-CSF were significantly elevated compared with non-inflammatory controls (FDR-adjusted P < 0.05). Four of 42 ANNA-1 positive samples with coexisting synaptic TIIFA staining were CAMKV-IgG positive. CAMKV-IgG is a paraneoplastic encephalitis autoantibody associated with diverse cancers. Neurologic improvement with immunotherapy is frequent, but prognosis is driven by cancer outcomes. Elevated IL-13 may indicate metastatic risk.

papers.abstract: Laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) poses significant clinical challenges due to pronounced tumor heterogeneity. To identify robust, consistent biomarkers across cohorts, we integrated bulk RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) data from GSE127165 and GSE142083 and validated candidate biomarkers in the external cohort GSE13060. Candidate gene prioritization incorporated differentially expressed genes, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) results, and markers of malignant epithelial cells exhibiting high copy number variation (High-CNV) derived from single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) (GSE206332). Additional analyses included functional enrichment, immune association (adjusted for tumor purity), quasi-temporal analysis, and CellChat inference to elucidate the biological roles of top genes. The integrated approach identified 254 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), comprising 86 upregulated and 168 downregulated genes. WGCNA revealed a tumor-associated module containing 870 genes. Intersecting these findings with high-CNV malignant epithelial markers reduced the candidate pool to 16 genes, and LASSO regression retained five key features: MYBL2, KRT17, UCHL1, PTHLH, and ODC1. Among these, MYBL2 demonstrated the strongest and most consistent performance. MYBL2 was further associated with proliferative programs, including E2F targets, the G2/M checkpoint, DNA repair, and MYC targets. Gene signatures from these subclusters were enriched in bulk tumors and positively correlated with MYBL2 expression in independent cohorts. The results also indicate that MYBL2-high malignant epithelial states are linked to distinct connectivity patterns within the tumor microenvironment.

papers.abstract: Multiple myeloma (MM) is a clonal plasma cell malignancy in which disease relapse and treatment resistance remain major clinical challenges. Identifying molecular dependencies that support myeloma cell fitness may reveal therapeutic vulnerabilities beyond recurrent genomic alterations. Mesencephalic astrocyte-derived neurotrophic factor (MANF) is an endoplasmic reticulum-resident, stress-responsive protein, but its clinical and biological significance in MM remains poorly defined. Publicly available DepMap CRISPR dependency data were analyzed to identify candidate MM-preferential dependencies. MANF expression and prognostic associations were examined in the MMRF CoMMpass cohort. Single-cell RNA sequencing and in silico perturbation analyses characterized its cellular distribution and predicted functional associations. MANF knockdown and genetic rescue using an siRNA-resistant MANF construct were performed in RPMI-8226 and OPM-2 cells to assess proliferation, cell-cycle distribution, and bortezomib sensitivity. Transcriptomic profiling characterized gene expression changes following MANF knockdown, while measurements at multiple time points assessed the temporal patterns of IRE1α-XBP1s-associated readouts. MANF was identified as a candidate MM-preferential dependency. Higher MANF expression was associated with advanced ISS stage and inferior overall survival, with the survival association retained after adjustment for established clinical and cytogenetic risk factors. Single-cell analysis localized MANF expression predominantly to plasma cells, while virtual knockout predicted changes involving ER protein processing, proteasome function, and metabolism. MANF knockdown inhibited proliferation, increased G0/G1 accumulation, and reduced MYC/E2F-associated transcriptional programs and cell-cycle regulatory proteins. Time-course analyses revealed early enhancement followed by later attenuation in selected IRE1α-XBP1s-associated readouts. MANF knockdown also increased bortezomib-induced apoptosis and reduced its IC₅₀. MANF re-expression partially reversed proliferation and cell-cycle phenotypes, restored IRE1α-XBP1s-associated protein abundance, and attenuated bortezomib sensitization. These findings identify MANF as a previously underexplored candidate myeloma-associated dependency that supports proliferative fitness and modulates bortezomib sensitivity in the tested MM models. MANF depletion is associated with dynamic changes in IRE1α-XBP1s-related readouts. These results support further investigation of MANF as a candidate therapeutic vulnerability in MM.

papers.abstract: Intraoperative cell salvage (CS) reduces allogeneic transfusion in cardiac surgery, but the washing process removes coagulation factors and platelets, raising hemostatic concerns. The dose-response relationship between CS volume and perioperative hemostatic changes remains poorly characterized. In this retrospective study of adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery with CS use, two cohorts with paired hemostatic measurements were identified: a routine coagulation cohort (primary analysis) and a viscoelastic cohort (exploratory analysis). Both cohorts were restricted to patients without coagulation-affecting blood products between measurements. Multivariable linear regression examined CS volume and absolute changes in each parameter, adjusted for surgical and patient characteristics and baseline values. In the routine coagulation cohort (N = 677; median CS 0.5 L, range 0.1-1.6 L), CS volume was not significantly associated with absolute changes in any parameter (all p ≥ 0.144). In the viscoelastic cohort (N = 50; median CS 0.8 L, range 0.2-3.7 L), CS volume was significantly associated with decreased functional fibrinogen clot strength (CFF MA: β = -3.31 mm/L; 95% CI: -5.53, -1.08; p = 0.004) and overall clot strength (CK MA: β = -2.93 mm/L; 95% CI: -5.73, -0.13; p = 0.041); after Holm correction for multiple testing, the CFF MA association remained significant (adjusted p = 0.031), whereas the CK MA association did not (adjusted p = 0.244). At observed reinfusion volumes, CS was not associated with changes in routine coagulation parameters, but in the exploratory viscoelastic cohort, higher CS volume was associated with lower functional fibrinogen clot strength. These findings highlight the potential value of viscoelastic monitoring when higher volumes are anticipated.

papers.abstract: Some patients with metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) receiving anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) progress at a few sites while disease elsewhere stays controlled, a pattern consistent with focal, oligo-acquired immune escape rather than systemic treatment failure. Ablating the escaping focus may eliminate the resistant clone and preserve an otherwise effective immunotherapy line. We performed a PRISMA 2020-compliant, PROSPERO-registered systematic review and meta-analysis of local ablative treatment (LAT) for oligoprogressive or oligo-resistant metastatic NSCLC during active ICI therapy, with continuation of the same immunotherapy line after LAT. MEDLINE, PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to March 8, 2026. From 1270 records, 22 studies were included in the qualitative synthesis. Four studies, one randomized subgroup, and three retrospective cohorts contributed to each primary analysis. LAT-oriented management was associated with improved progression-free survival (PFS; pooled hazard ratio [HR] 0.45, 95% CI 0.33-0.62; 95% prediction interval [PI] 0.28-0.74; I2 = 0%) and overall survival (OS; pooled HR 0.41, 95% CI 0.27-0.63; 95% PI 0.24-0.69; I2 = 0%). PFS and OS estimates were consistent across sensitivity analyses, including the exclusion of the one PFS estimate measured to a second progression. The evidence is predominantly observational and of low certainty, reflecting the current absence of NSCLC-specific randomized trials. On this evidence, LAT, delivered predominantly as stereotactic body radiotherapy, may be considered a continuation-enabling option for carefully selected patients with focal progression on otherwise effective immunotherapy, pending ongoing randomized trials.

papers.abstract: Abstract Background Coping behavior is an important component of psychological adaptation in patients with brain neoplasms, whose illness may involve neurological deficits, cognitive impairment, prognostic uncertainty, and threats to autonomy and personal identity. However, evidence on coping patterns across different types of brain tumors and their relationships with quality of life, affective state, and post-traumatic growth remains limited. Aim To examine the characteristics of coping behavior in patients with brain neoplasms and to assess the associations between specific coping strategies and quality of life, affective state, and post-traumatic growth. Materials and methods The study included 102 patients with brain neoplasms treated in neurosurgical departments in the Republic of Uzbekistan (Mage = 42.5, SD = 15.35; 52 women and 50 men). Patients were divided into three groups according to the histological type of neoplasm: meningiomas ( n = 34), glioneuronal tumors ( n = 35), and other neoplasms ( n = 33). Coping behavior was assessed using the brief version of the COPE-30 questionnaire and an additional Meaning-Focused Coping Scale. Quality of life was assessed using the EORTC QLQ-C30 questionnaire and its brain cancer-specific module, QLQ-BN20. Anxiety and depression were assessed using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), and post-traumatic growth was assessed using the Post-Traumatic Growth Inventory (PTGI). Results Active coping was the most frequently used strategy in the overall sample, whereas mental disengagement was the least frequently used. Patients with meningiomas more frequently reported active coping, planning, and meaning-focused coping, whereas religious coping and humor were relatively more common among patients with glioneuronal tumors. Meaning-focused coping was positively associated with post-traumatic growth, satisfaction with health, and emotional functioning, and negatively associated with depressive symptoms. Its association with anxiety was not statistically significant. Discussion The findings suggest that coping behavior represents an important component of the subjective experience of illness in patients with brain tumors. In the present study, the greatest adaptive potential was observed for coping strategies involving active patient engagement in managing the illness and reappraising its personal meaning. Conclusion Assessment of coping strategies in patients with brain neoplasms may have clinical relevance for psychological support and could inform the development of differentiated psychosocial intervention programs.

papers.abstract: Abstract Purpose Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most aggressive primary brain tumor with poor outcomes despite surgery, radiotherapy (RT), and temozolomide (TMZ). Monitoring relies on imaging, which is confounded by pseudoprogression and provides limited molecular insight. Circulating biomarkers may offer a minimally invasive approach to track disease and treatment effects. Methods We performed targeted longitudinal proteomic profiling of plasma from post-surgery GBM patients ( n = 11) at baseline (pre-radiotherapy (RT)), after RT with concomitant TMZ, and after adjuvant TMZ, alongside healthy controls ( n = 15), using the NULISAseq CNS panel covering 131 proteins related to neurodegeneration, neuroinflammation, and vascular health. Differential expressions were assessed using volcano plots, hierarchical clustering, paired statistical comparisons and longitudinal trends analysis. Results At baseline, GBM plasma showed elevated markers of neuroaxonal and glial injury, extracellular matrix regulators, and inflammatory signaling compared to controls. Several established neurodegeneration and Alzheimer’s disease- related biomarkers were also higher in GBM plasma versus controls. Following radiotherapy and concomitant TMZ, cytokines including IL10, IL5, and IL33 increased, indicating systemic immune activation, while BDNF showed a modest decline. Adjuvant TMZ treatment attenuated radiotherapy-induced cytokine elevations and reduced neuronal injury markers, suggesting therapy-driven reduction of inflammatory and neurodegenerative signals. Longitudinal analysis confirmed dynamic shifts in specific proteins across baseline, radiotherapy, and TMZ phases. Conclusion High-sensitivity plasma proteomics suggested therapy-induced changes in CNS-specific and immune markers in GBM, highlighting candidate biomarkers that can be further developed for real-time monitoring of treatment response. These findings suggest candidate circulating markers that may complement imaging for monitoring disease biology and therapeutic response, and warrant validation in larger cohorts.

papers.abstract: Local tumor excision (LTE) and segmental resection (SR) represent the two principal kidney-sparing surgery (KSS) modalities for upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC), yet the optimal procedure remains undefined. We compared their long-term survival outcomes and developed a tailored prognostic tool to guide individualized surgical decision-making. A cohort of patients with UTUC managed via KSS was identified from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results database and stratified into LTE and SR cohorts. Following propensity score matching to mitigate baseline confounding, long-term overall survival and cancer-specific survival were compared. Independent predictors derived from multivariable Cox regression analyses were subsequently integrated to develop a prognostic nomogram, which underwent external validation in an independent, real-world cohort. Following propensity score matching (n = 312), SR was associated with improved survival outcomes compared with LTE. Multivariable analysis confirmed SR as an independent predictor of improved overall survival (hazard ratio 0.657, P = 0.005) and cancer-specific survival (hazard ratio 0.592, P = 0.019), and this prognostic benefit remained robust across all clinical subgroups (all P for interaction > 0.05). The derived prognostic nomogram showed favorable performance during external validation, achieving a peak area under the curve of 0.852 during external validation and improving individualized risk assessment for patients in the KSS setting. For patients with localized UTUC undergoing KSS, our findings suggest that SR may be associated with favorable long-term survival outcomes compared with LTE. In addition, the externally validated nomogram showed satisfactory predictive performance and may serve as a useful tool for individualized risk stratification and clinical decision-making.

papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction The objective of the study is to create a bibliometric profile for recent graduates of complex general surgical oncology (CGSO) fellows to understand their very early career trajectory and inform the current training paradigm. Methods Bibliometric profiling of applicants to our CGSO fellowship program from 2017 to 2021 who completed an accredited program were included. Impact factors were adjusted for authorship position and type of publication. Results Among 232 CGSO graduates, 106 (45.7%) were female, 118 (50.9%) practice at a university-based flagship hospital (UBFH), 57 (43.2%) published, on average, more than 2 manuscripts per year after at least 2 years in independent practice. The median years in independent practice were 3 years (range 1-5 years). As they progressed in their training and career, the proportions of graduates who published, their level of involvement, the type, and quality of their publications evolved. Only 24 (10.3%) graduates published in basic science or translational research studies after fellowship. In a linear regression model, institution type (estimated means UBFH 7.1 vs. non-UBFH 2.8, p < 0.001), publications before fellowship (β coefficient 14, p < 0.001), publications during fellowship (β coefficient 0.33, p < 0.001), and years since graduating fellowship (β coefficient 2.52, p < 0.001) were associated with more publications during independent practice. Conclusion Majority of CGSO graduates do not consistently publish after fellowship. a minority of them engage in basic science or translational research despite great emphasis during fellowship application. A dual-track model to differentiate clinical and research-oriented fellows is needed.

papers.abstract: The advent of immunotherapy has profoundly transformed the therapeutic landscape of hematologic malignancies. A broad range of immune-based strategies, including immune checkpoint inhibitors and adoptive cell therapies based on both T cells and natural killer (NK) cells, have achieved unprecedented clinical outcomes in several lymphoid and myeloid neoplasms. Emerging approaches such as genetically engineered immune cells, including chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-modified T and NK cells, are further expanding therapeutic opportunities. However, substantial heterogeneity in treatment response remains a major challenge, with a significant proportion of patients experiencing primary resistance, relapse, or severe immune-related toxicities. Accurate identification of predictive and prognostic biomarkers is therefore essential to optimize patient selection, improve therapeutic efficacy, and minimize treatment-related toxicity. Numerous biological parameters have been investigated, including clinical prognostic scores, systemic inflammatory indices, tumor burden markers, immune-cell subsets, cytokine profiles, genetic and molecular alterations, and features of the tumor microenvironment. Emerging evidence indicates that both host-related factors and tumor-intrinsic characteristics shape therapeutic responses to immunotherapy across hematologic cancers. Among the most promising biomarkers are inflammatory indices derived from peripheral blood counts, such as the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, prognostic nutritional index, and Glasgow Prognostic Score. In parallel, immune-monitoring approaches assessing the functional competence, phenotype, and activation status of both T and NK cells, together with cytokine signatures, immune checkpoint expression, and other markers of immune competence, are increasingly recognized as valuable tools for predicting therapeutic response, resistance, and immune-related toxicity. This review summarizes the current evidence on prognostic scores and biomarkers associated with immunotherapy outcomes in hematologic malignancies. We discuss their biological rationale, clinical relevance, current limitations, and potential integration into contemporary treatment strategies. Finally, we highlight emerging perspectives, including multi-omics profiling, artificial intelligence-driven predictive models, and dynamic biomarker-guided approaches, which are expected to advance precision immuno-oncology and enable increasingly personalized immune-based treatment algorithms.

papers.abstract: Abstract Background Ischaemic stroke occurs when blood flow to the brain is obstructed. Rapid restoration of blood supply frequently induces cerebral ischaemia‒reperfusion injury (CIRI). Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cell (BMSC)‐derived exosomes exhibit promising therapeutic potential for CIRI. In‐depth exploration of their therapeutic mechanisms holds crucial significance for CIRI management. Methods The middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO) model was established in mice. An in vitro ischaemic stroke model was established by treating BV‐2 cells with oxygen‒glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R). Exosomes were isolated from BMSCs and intranasally administrated into mice or added into BV‐2 cells. Neurological deficits, grasping and coordination function were evaluated. Cell viability, apoptosis, proliferation and migration were examined. The localisation of KLF3‐AS1 was examined by combined staining of immunofluorescence and fluorescence in situ hybridisation. Intracellular Ca 2+ and adenosine triphosphate levels, mitochondrial reactive oxygen species and membrane potential were assessed. Results KLF3‐AS1 enhanced BMSC viability, proliferation and migration, accompanied by epigenetic reprogramming at its promoter characterised by increased H3K27 acetylation (H3K27Ac) and decreased H3K27 trimethylation (H3K27Me3). BMSC‐derived KLF3‐AS1‐enriched exosomes indicated therapeutic efficacy in both in vivo and in vitro models of cerebral ischaemia. In MCAO‐induced mice, these exosomes alleviated neurological deficits and shifted microglial polarisation from pro‐inflammatory M1‐like to anti‐inflammatory M2‐like phenotypes. Similar effects were observed in OGD/R‐treated BV‐2 microglia, where KLF3‐AS1‐enriched exosomes attenuated oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction while upregulating Silent Information Regulator 3 (SIRT3) expression. Mechanistically, KLF3‐AS1 facilitated ETS Variant Transcription Factor 4 (ETV4) nuclear translocation to activate SIRT3 transcription in microglia, and inhibition of SIRT3 abolished the neuroprotective effects of exosomal KLF3‐AS1. Conclusion BMSC‐derived exosomes delivering KLF3‐AS1 ameliorates CIRI by preserving microglial mitochondrial function and inhibiting inflammatory polarisation, highlighting KLF3‐AS1 as a critical epigenetic regulator and exosome‐mediated therapeutic agent for CIRI through the ETV4/SIRT3 axis. Key points/Highlights KLF3‐AS1 enhances bone marrow mesenchymal stem cell (BMSC) function via promoter H3K27Ac/H3K27Me3 reprogramming. KLF3‑AS1 directly binds ETS Variant Transcription Factor 4 (ETV4) to activate Silent Information Regulator 3 (SIRT3), preserving mitochondrial integrity. BMSC‑derived exosomal KLF3‑AS1 promotes M2 microglial polarisation and ameliorates cerebral ischaemia–reperfusion injury.
